business-data-context · Bunkai TMS

Business data map

Built 2026-10-12 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 98ee1b4 (2026-10-11) and the live database through the read-only QA role. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

What Bunkai is at the data level. Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. Every row belongs to a workspace (the tenant). Inside it, a team describes the product under test as projects split into a tree of modules, writes user stories with ordered acceptance criteria, and authors ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases: small, reusable checks made of steps and assertions) that must be anchored to a story and at least one of its criteria. ATCs are chained into Tests; a Test is executed as a Run against a project environment; a Run copies the chain at start and records a result per step; failures become bugs. Test plans and milestones organise the work (a plan can be closed with a verdict, a milestone tracks the readiness of its attached plans); reports (coverage, traceability, defect heatmap, recovery cycles, run report, plan progress, milestone readiness) are read straight from these tables. Since 2026-10-12 the same data is also reachable by automation (automated run submission, streamed step results, bulk ATC edit), discussed by the team in a workspace chat, and mirrored toward Jira through a per-workspace connection.

Actors. Browser users (cookie session, roles viewer / member / admin / owner per workspace); programmatic callers (CLI, CI, AI agents) with a personal access token bk_pat_… carrying scopes; system principals: four pg_cron jobs inside Postgres, two Vercel Cron calls (daily digest and daily storage cleanup, bearer CRON_SECRET), and the Stripe webhook (signature-verified).

How data is written. Nearly every business mutation goes through a Postgres function (RPC) that validates, authorises, writes the rows and an activity_log audit row in one transaction. Route handlers under app/api/v1/ call those RPCs either as the user (RLS-scoped client) or through the admin client passing the resolved actor explicitly. Postgres Row Level Security is the authorisation source of truth; the shared database now has 53 tables in public (was 38), all with RLS enabled, 27 user-defined triggers (was 14) and four pg_cron jobs (was two). Membership writes (workspace_members) no longer have any user-session write path: only locked RPCs change them.

Value proposition the data enforces. Traceability is structural: an ATC cannot exist without a user story and at least one of that story's criteria, a Run keeps an immutable snapshot of what was executed, and a bug keeps provenance links to the run, failed step and ATC it came from. That chain (criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug) is what the traceability and coverage reports read. Archiving is reversible for Modules, ATCs and Milestones, and always hides rather than deletes.

Scale in the shared database (dbhub, read-only role, 2026-11-17). 3,105 workspaces (1,215 soft-deleted), 3,964 projects, 21,720 ATCs (50 archived), 3,691 Tests, 4,684 Runs (4,576 human, 81 agent, 27 ci), 3,145 bugs and 58 chat messages. Plans: 3,096 community, 1 cloud, 8 enterprise. Most of it is QA and automation test data.

External services. Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage with the private bucket run-evidence, Vault, pg_cron), Stripe (plan upgrade checkout, billing details, invoices, payment-method replacement, failed-renewal grace), Resend (digest and deletion emails), Jira Cloud (one-way story import through a per-workspace connection; bug sync is configured but nothing sends yet), Vercel (hosting, background after() workers, two crons).

Key relationships

  • A workspace owns projects and Tests directly. Tests are workspace-scoped on purpose: a Test has no project column; its project is derived from the ATCs it chains (test_steps to atcs to projects), so one chain may span two projects.
  • A project owns its module tree, milestones, test plans, environments and its tracker settings. Modules hold user stories; a story holds ordered acceptance criteria.
  • An ATC belongs to one project and one module and is anchored to exactly one user story (atcs.user_story_id, ON DELETE RESTRICT) and bound to one or more of that story's criteria through atc_acceptance_criteria (many-to-many).
  • A Test chains ATCs through test_steps by reference, in order; the same ATC may appear at several positions. test_steps.atc_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT.
  • A test plan holds a Test at most once (test_plan_tests). A milestone references plans through milestone_plans (a reference, never a copy; one plan may serve several milestones, at most 50 per milestone).
  • A Run belongs to one Test and one environment (both RESTRICT), snapshots the chain into run_atcs and run_steps, and records the module of chain position 1 as runs.module_id. Each run_atcs row also keeps source_atc_id, the ATC key that survives an ATC delete, so two Runs can be compared. Step attachments hang off a run step.
  • A bug always has a workspace, project and module; its run_id, run_step_id and atc_id are optional provenance links. Evidence uploads hang off the bug and the project.
  • Notifications and activity rows hang off the workspace; a notification links to its producing activity row through source_event_id, or to a chat message for mentions.
  • A workspace has one general chat channel (created by a trigger); messages carry a strictly increasing seq and optional mention rows; a mention produces one in-app notification per mentioned member.
  • A workspace has at most one Jira connection and one billing state (profile, payment state and grace period); a project has at most one tracker settings row, and the connection check of those settings uses the workspace's Jira connection. Saved views belong to a person and a project.
  • An automated submission stores its idempotency key per workspace and returns the first Run for a retry. Deleting a run step attachment or a bug evidence upload queues its Storage object in the cleanup queue, which a daily job drains (up to 10 attempts per object).

Workspace and membership

  • Tenant boundary. Every table reaches a workspace_id directly or through its parent; the four RLS helpers (bunkai_is_workspace_member, _admin, _owner, bunkai_can_write_workspace) and the explicit-actor helpers used by admin-client routes all require an active membership in a live workspace.
  • Creation. bunkai_bootstrap_workspace inserts the workspace and the caller's owner membership in one transaction; the slug is globally unique and a collision is an error. New workspaces start on the community plan.
  • Plan tier (plan: community / cloud / enterprise). The tier ladder lives in TypeScript (lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts, unchanged): Community 5 seats, 3 projects, 30-day retention, free; Cloud 25 seats, 50 projects, 90 days, 24.00 USD per seat; Enterprise unlimited, custom price. Only the project limit is enforced, by a trigger on projects, and it now evaluates the EFFECTIVE plan (bunkai_effective_plan): a Cloud workspace whose unpaid-renewal grace window has ended is judged as Community from that exact instant while workspaces.plan keeps saying cloud. See entity-billing-state.
  • Soft delete. deleted_at + deletion_requested_by mark a workspace scheduled for deletion; from that instant every helper treats it as non-existent. A restore is refused once the 30-day window closed (see state-workspace).
  • Membership. role viewer / member / admin / owner; status active / invited / suspended, but only active is ever written by code. Roles form a ladder (viewer 1, member 2, admin 3, owner 4). Nobody can write workspace_members through a user session any more: the INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE policies and privileges were dropped, and every change goes through locked RPCs (bootstrap, invite accept, leave, remove). A workspace can have several owners.
  • Removing a teammate (bunkai_remove_workspace_member) is one transaction: unassign the target's bugs, revoke their workspace-scoped tokens (global tokens stay), revoke pending invites addressed to them, delete the membership, audit member.removed. An admin cannot remove an owner (45221) and nobody can remove themselves this way (45220, that is Leave).
  • Leaving counts only memberships in LIVE workspaces: a membership in a workspace scheduled for deletion no longer counts as "another workspace" for the last-membership guard.

Module tree

  • Self-referencing tree with a materialised slash path (for example auth/login), unique per project, depth 1 to 6 enforced by a CHECK. An optional description is capped at 500 characters.
  • Rename rebuilds the path of the module and every descendant in one statement; a sibling slug collision is rejected. Move re-parents and re-bases the subtree, rejecting cycles, a parent in another project or archived, and any move that would push a descendant beyond depth 6. A module.renamed event is written only when the name or rebuilt path really changed, and module.description_updated only when the description really changed (the edit form submits both fields on every save).
  • Archive hides a whole branch. bunkai_archive_module_subtree stamps archived_at on the module, its descendants, their user stories, criteria and ATCs with one timestamp and one archive_batch_id (new column on modules, user_stories, acceptance_criteria and atcs). Tests, runs and bugs are not touched: a bug filed against an archived module stays readable and is tagged "Archived".
  • Restore is the exact inverse of ONE archive (bunkai_restore_module_subtree, POST /modules/{id}/restore): it brings back the rows that archive took, found through the batch id. Rows archived on their own or before 0117 (batch id null) are never swept up. Audited as module.restored.
  • Module creation is a plain RLS-checked insert (no RPC, no audit row); rename, description change, move, archive and restore each write an activity row.

User story and acceptance criteria

  • A story belongs to a module and carries a denormalised project_id. external_id (a Jira key) and external_url link it to a tracker; the key is unique per project among active stories, case-insensitive, so an archived story never blocks re-linking.
  • Criteria are ordered by position, unique among active rows; insert, move and archive go through RPCs that rebalance positions atomically.
  • status is draft or ready_to_test. Moving to ready_to_test requires at least one active criterion (serialised with a row lock against criterion archiving); archiving the last active criterion drops the story back to draft. The status is shown in the sidebar and traceability view; no other workflow is gated on it.
  • A story with ATCs attached cannot be hard-deleted (RESTRICT from atcs); the DELETE endpoint archives through bunkai_archive_user_story, which in one transaction and with one timestamp archives the story, its live criteria and its live ATCs. Before 0111 only the story was archived and its ATCs stayed readable by id. There is no story restore path; a story restored with its Module returns only if it was archived by that Module archive.

ATC (Acceptance Test Case)

  • Name. The code, UI and app metadata expand ATC as "Acceptance Test Case".
  • Identity. slug is minted at create as {module-slug}/atc-{8 hex}; user_story_id is immutable on edit. module_id is still never changed by a single edit, but a bulk edit can move an ATC to another module inside its story's module subtree: the module segment of the slug is regenerated and the 8-hex suffix is kept.
  • Content. Ordered steps (action, optional input data, expected result) and ordered assertions; both are replaced as a whole on every save. layer is UI / API / Unit; optional technique and priority (Critical / High / Medium / Low). Title at least 3 characters; at most 10 tags, enforced in the RPC and by a CHECK.
  • Versioning. Every update bumps version and requires the caller's version (optimistic lock, 409 on mismatch). The atc.updated audit row lists the Tests that chain the ATC; those Tests show the new content on their next read because they hold references, not copies.
  • Archive on its own. bunkai_archive_atc / bunkai_restore_atc stamp archived_at and archived_by (null when a parent's cascade archived it), idempotent, one atc.archived / atc.restored event per real change. An archived ATC cannot be edited or duplicated (45025). It stays as evidence: coverage and traceability still count what it produced, and a criterion bound only to archived ATCs is not "uncovered". Restore under an archived parent hands the ATC to the parent's cascade state instead of clearing the column (reuse reads rely on "archived parent means archived children").
  • Bulk edit. bunkai_bulk_edit_atcs changes ONE field (tags add or remove, module, layer or priority) on up to 200 ATCs per call, one subtransaction per ATC: each outcome is changed, unchanged or refused with a reason (not_found, archived, stale_version, tags_limit_exceeded, module_outside_story_subtree, slug_conflict, write_failed). A no-op is a success evaluated before the stale check; a dry run reports refusals with no write.
  • Dead column. atcs.status (pass / fail / blocked / skipped / running / unrun) defaults to unrun and no code path writes it; execution truth lives in run_atcs.status. I did not re-measure its values on 2026-11-17.
  • Search. A stored tsv column over title and tags (kept fresh by a trigger) backs project-scoped full-text search.

Test (chain of ATCs)

  • A Test is a workspace-scoped header (title 1 to 200 characters, trimmed) plus an ordered chain in test_steps. Creation requires a non-empty chain of ATCs from the same workspace.
  • The chain stores references only. Reading a Test expands each ATC live with its current steps and assertions and now tells which chain steps hold an archived ATC (archived_at per step); the frozen copy belongs to Runs.
  • Reorder must keep exactly the same multiset of ATCs and is guarded by the Test's version. Tags replace the whole set: reserved suite tags smoke, sanity, regression are lower-cased, custom tags keep their casing.
  • The tag lookup (GET /tests?tag=) returns one bounded keyset page (1 to 50 per page, ordered by creation time then id) with an opaque next cursor.
  • automation_status is manual-only (default), candidate or automated, CHECK-constrained. Every Test (3,691) is manual-only: no write path ships; chat rich links read it.
  • "Used in N tests" for an ATC counts distinct Tests that chain it.

Run (execution snapshot)

  • The header snapshots test_title and the module of chain position 1 at start; executor_mode is human / agent / ci and executor_user_id is the starter (the only recipient of run notifications).
  • Provenance of automated runs: executor_token_id (the PAT that started or submitted the run), executor_name (token name snapshot, fallback "API token") and evidence_urls (http or https links, at most 20).
  • run_atcs copies each chain position (ATC title, position) plus source_atc_id, a plain uuid without foreign key that survives an ATC delete; run_steps copies each ATC step. Links back to the live ATC and step are provenance only.
  • Per-step result: status, note, evidence_url, executed_at. A person re-marking a step is last write wins; a bearer (API) caller re-reporting an identical result is a no-op, and a different result for an already reported step is a conflict (45239).
  • Attachments: up to 10 screenshots per step in run_step_attachments (see entity-evidence-attachment).
  • runs has no archive and no delete path; it grows by one row per execution. Realtime still replicates run_atcs and run_steps, not runs.

Bug

  • Title 5 to 200 characters, severity P1 to P4, optional description and steps to reproduce, evidence, reporter (created_by) and optional assignee. Evidence is a combined list of links and uploaded screenshots, at most 10 items and 50 MiB of uploads in total (45303).
  • Filed from a failed run step (the API derives project, module, run and ATC server-side from run_step_id) or standalone (shown as "Filed manually").
  • Consistency is enforced twice: by the create RPC and by the bugs_check_consistency trigger (module in project, project in workspace, provenance, status moves, assignee eligibility).
  • content_version (starts at 1) is the staleness token for corrections: bunkai_correct_bug (title, severity, description, steps) requires the version the caller loaded (45314 when stale) and bumps it only on an effective change, so status and assignee changes never make a content save stale. Corrections are audited as bug.corrected.
  • Jira sync state columns (sync_state not_applicable / pending / syncing / synced / failed, external_issue_key, external_issue_url, attempt counters, last error, next attempt, claim time) exist since 0091. All 3,145 bugs read not_applicable; I found no code that sends a bug to Jira (see discovery-gaps).
  • bugs is in the Realtime publication (the Defect Heatmap updates itself when a defect is filed), filtered by the subscriber's own read policy.
  • Bugs have no archive and no delete path.

Activity log (audit and event source)

  • Clients cannot insert: only SECURITY DEFINER RPCs and triggers write it, inside the same transaction as the change, so a failed write leaves no audit row.
  • Actions seen in the database in the earlier snapshot: atc.created, atc.updated, test.created, test.reordered, test.tags_changed, run.started, run.finished, run.aborted, run_step.marked, bug.filed, bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.unassigned, bug.status_changed, module.renamed, module.description_updated, module.moved, module.archived, milestone.created, milestone.updated, test_plan.created, test_plan.updated, test_plan.tests_added, test_plan.test_removed, export.requested, export.downloaded.
  • Added by migrations 0095 to 0130 (read from migration text; I did not count rows): test_plan.closed, test_plan.reopened, atc.archived, atc.restored, module.restored, milestone.archived, milestone.restored, member.removed, bug.corrected, jira_connection.connected, jira_connection.changed, jira_connection.disconnected (payload only the site host, never token, secret id or email). atc.updated is also written once per ATC changed by a bulk edit.
  • The activity feed (bunkai_list_activity) returns a per-action positive projection of the payload, never the raw payload, behind an allowlist; atc.updated shows up to 3 affected Test titles, module.archived / module.restored show the Module name, member.removed resolves the removed person as an actor. Terminal run events carry via (cookie, bearer or sweep).
  • Two AFTER INSERT triggers turn run and bug events into notifications (see flow-notifications).

Notification and preferences

  • One row per recipient, workspace-scoped, with a payload snapshot so the inbox renders without joining live entities. Unique per (producing activity row, recipient): a replay never double-notifies.
  • A recipient sees only their own rows of the last 90 days while still an active member (RLS), excluding rows flagged in_app_suppressed. Mark-read is a plain update of read_at.
  • Event types produced: run.finished, run.aborted, bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.status_changed, and mentions (entity type chat_message, payload message id, channel, author, 140-character snippet). bug.unassigned reaches the trigger but has no recipient.
  • Preferences are personal and global: run_lifecycle and bug_lifecycle times in_app and email, default on when no row exists; mentions cells stay locked (mentions are always delivered in-app regardless). Both channels are now honoured at write time: in-app off flags the new row in_app_suppressed (hidden from inbox, bell and realtime); email on still delivers it in the next daily digest; both off stores nothing. The decision is a snapshot at event time, toggling later changes nothing already stored.
  • emailed_at is stamped by the digest runner after a successful send so an email-only (suppressed) row is digested once; visible rows keep being included while unread.

Personal access token

  • Shown once as bk_pat_{prefix}.{secret}; only a SHA-256 of the secret is stored, in a sibling secret table the QA inspection roles cannot read. Lookup is by a 12-character prefix.
  • Scopes: atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (at least one). workspace:admin can only be granted to an admin or owner of the token's workspace; a token with no workspace is global (a global token cannot submit an automated run: 45238).
  • Issued only from a browser session or by the headless sign-in and confirm endpoints; a PAT cannot mint or revoke tokens. Revocation stamps revoked_at (no delete, for audit). Leaving the workspace, being removed from it, or workspace deletion revokes the workspace-scoped tokens.
  • A PAT call acts as its owner: the API mints a short-lived user JWT so RLS sees the same auth.uid() as a browser call. A run started or submitted with a token stores the token id and name on the run as provenance.

Workspace invite

  • An admin or owner invites an email with role viewer, member or admin; inviting an existing active member is rejected. The raw token is returned once inside the accept URL; only its hash is stored. Bunkai sends no invite email: the inviter shares the link.
  • State is derived from timestamps, not a status column: pending, accepted, revoked, expired (expires_at, default 7 days). Rotating issues a fresh secret and expiry for the same row.
  • Accepting requires a signed-in user whose email equals the invite email; it adds or upgrades the membership. Since 0118 accept is one transaction (bunkai_accept_workspace_invite) that re-validates the inviter under lock and fails closed, and a user session can no longer rewrite who issued an invite, to whom it is addressed or its role.
  • Removing a member revokes the pending invites addressed to that person.

Team chat (channel, messages, mentions)

  • Channel. One general channel per workspace (chat_channels.kind = general), created by a trigger on workspaces and backfilled. The table is ready for a later per-project kind.
  • Ordering. chat_messages.seq is a bigint identity: a total order stable under concurrent sends; pagination and reconnect catch-up are keyset on it. Messages reach open browsers through Supabase Realtime (chat_messages is in the publication, RLS gates delivery).
  • Access. Any active member reads; member, admin and owner write; viewers are read-only. Clients cannot update or delete rows: writes go through bunkai_chat_send_message, bunkai_chat_edit_message and bunkai_chat_delete_message, which take the actor from auth.uid().
  • Edit and delete. An author may edit within 15 minutes. Delete is a soft delete: the row stays as a tombstone (reply context and order survive) and body is overwritten with an empty string, so the original text is gone for every reader and every realtime payload. Author and moderator deletions are indistinguishable: no deleted_by is stored.
  • Mentions. chat_message_mentions (message, workspace, mentioned user) is the source of truth for pills and notifications; the body keeps the readable "@Name". Ids that are not active members of the workspace are dropped silently, duplicates collapse, at most 50 are considered. One mentions notification per mentioned member per message, always in-app, never for a self-mention. An edit notifies only ADDED members; removed mentions delete their row; deleting a message removes its mention rows. A member who left keeps a named pill on old messages.
  • Rich links. POST /workspaces/{id}/chat/entities/resolve (up to 20 references) turns links to an ATC, Test or Run of the same workspace into cards (Test card shows the persisted automation status); an entity in another workspace answers restricted with no data, an unreadable or missing one unavailable. GET .../chat/entities/search offers 5 candidates per type. GET .../chat/roster lists members for the mention picker.

Saved view

  • The old user_view_state (one unnamed row per person, project and surface) was reshaped in place into SEVERAL NAMED views. Surfaces: traceability, run_history, bugs, workbench. Rows outside that set, or whose state was not a non-empty object or exceeded 4096 bytes, were deleted by the migration; 31 views exist in the shared database.
  • Owner-only: plain table CRUD through the caller's RLS client (user_id = auth.uid()), no SECURITY DEFINER function. Invariants live in the database: unique name per person, project and surface (case and NFC normalised by the API), a cap of 25 views per surface (45100) and immutable owner, project, surface and creation time (45101).
  • Routes: GET/POST /projects/{id}/saved-views and /saved-views/{viewId} (read needs atc:read, write atc:write).

Milestone and attached plans

  • A milestone is a named target date in a project. Plans are attached through milestone_plans, a reference (detaching never touches the plan), one plan may serve several milestones, unique per (milestone, plan), at most 50 plans per milestone. Member or above writes; a plan from another project or workspace, or a missing one, is one indistinguishable refusal (45505). Attaching several plans is all-or-nothing; detaching an unattached plan succeeds without a write.
  • Readiness. bunkai_milestones_readiness pools the counts of all attached plans and reports floor(sum passed x 100 / sum tests): 100 only when every pooled test passed, never a mean of plan percentages. A closed plan contributes the progress it froze at close; an open plan its live progress.
  • Archive hides, never deletes. milestones.archived_at / archived_by; archive and restore are idempotent, one event per real change (milestone.archived, milestone.restored). An archived milestone cannot be edited, nor have plans attached or detached (45507), and a name held by an archived milestone blocks a new one with that name (45508). A trigger makes the archived row read-only for any writer.
  • Before 0112 no entity linked to milestones.

Evidence attachments and storage cleanup

  • Two kinds of screenshot evidence share one private Storage bucket run-evidence: attachments of a run step (run_step_attachments) and uploads made while filing a defect (bug_evidence_attachments, key prefix {workspace}/bug/{project}/{attachment}). PNG, JPEG or WebP, 1 byte to 10 MiB per file, no client Storage policy: objects are read and written only by the service role after an RPC or RLS check.
  • Run step attachments: at most 10 per step, 50 MiB per step, 250 MiB per Run. Member, admin or owner attach; only the uploader removes, and only while the Run is running; every member reads; a closed Run is read-only forever (45216). Limits raise 45217 with a reason (step_count, step_bytes, run_bytes, file_bytes).
  • Bug evidence: links plus uploads, at most 10 items and 50 MiB. An upload is private to the person who made it until the defect is filed, expires 3 hours after creation if unclaimed, and is frozen once claimed by exactly one bug (45317); the filing request carries the order of the combined list.
  • Upload path: init (RPC creates a pending row and a signed upload URL) then the browser PUTs the bytes straight to Storage (they never cross a Vercel Function) then commit (RPC verifies and makes the row visible).
  • Cleanup. An AFTER DELETE trigger on each attachment table queues the object in storage_cleanup_queue. The daily route GET /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup (Vercel Cron 03:00 UTC) expires stale pending rows, deletes queued objects (batch 200, up to 10 attempts, then stuck) and purges finished queue rows older than 7 days.

Workspace Jira connection and project tracker settings

  • Workspace connection (workspace_jira_connections): Jira site URL (must be https://<name>.atlassian.net, 45420), account email (45421) and API token. The token lives in Supabase Vault and the table keeps only the Vault secret id; no RPC or route returns the token. Only the service role reads or writes the table; a BEFORE DELETE trigger removes the Vault secret, also when the workspace cascades. This reverses the earlier rule "no credential in the database" for workspace credentials, because one deployment now serves many workspaces.
  • Who: owner or admin write (workspace:admin plus a live role read); a token is required whenever the site changes or no connection exists (45422), so a stored token cannot be repointed to another host. Connect, change and disconnect are audited (jira_connection.*, site host only). There is no environment fallback any more.
  • Project tracker settings (project_tracker_settings, one row per project): destination Jira project key (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,9}$, 45410/45411), issue type up to 60 characters (45412) and an on/off switch. No column can hold a secret. Admins save through bunkai_upsert_project_tracker_settings (service role only), serialised per project by an advisory lock; saving with the sync on re-queues the project's stranded bugs (those without an external key that are failed, or not_applicable and open or in progress) as pending, and the caller must confirm the exact count first (45413, 45414). The save is audited in the same transaction.
  • POST /projects/{id}/tracker-settings/check and /workspaces/{id}/jira-connection/check test the connection or destination against Jira.

Billing profile, payment state and grace period

  • workspace_billing_profiles: company name, billing email and address the owner maintains; the app pushes every save to the Stripe Customer, which holds the copy printed on invoices.
  • workspace_billing_state: workspace to Stripe customer and subscription mapping (created when a checkout completes), a payment-method SUMMARY (brand, last four, expiry, never a card number) and payment_state (paid, payment_failed, retry_pending, recovered). Readable by owner and admin only.
  • workspace_grace_periods: the 14-day grace window of an unpaid renewal (start and end). Kept apart because any active member may read it: the project-limit trigger is SECURITY INVOKER and must evaluate it.
  • bunkai_effective_plan is a pure function: a Cloud workspace whose grace window ended is treated as Community from the exact instant (now >= end), with no sweep job. workspaces.plan stays cloud and nothing is deleted.
  • No client write policy exists on these tables: all writes go through the service role after the owner check, or through two webhook-only RPCs (invoice event and payment-method event), idempotent per Stripe event id with a stale-event guard for out-of-order delivery.

Flow: sign-in and first workspace

  • Email-first entry: POST /api/v1/auth/check-email asks auth_email_status (service role only) whether the account exists and is confirmed. Account existence is knowingly disclosed, mitigated by an app-level rate limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds and 60 per hour per network source.
  • The rate limiter (bunkai_rate_limit_consume) keeps one row per ALLOWED hit in rate_limit_hits (sliding log), under a per-key advisory lock so concurrent requests cannot exceed the budget; keys are HMAC digests of the source (taken only from headers Vercel asserts; otherwise one shared unknown bucket) or of the lower-cased email, never raw values. An hourly pg_cron job sweeps expired rows. The credential endpoints (password sign-in and sign-up code confirm) use the same per-source budget plus 10 attempts per 15 minutes per account.
  • Sign-in paths: magic link (POST /auth/magic-link, each link audited in magic_link_tokens), OAuth with GitHub or Google (state cookie, PKCE, /auth/callback), or headless email + password (POST /auth/signin), which also mints a PAT in the same call.
  • Headless sign-up (POST /auth/signup) creates the user unconfirmed; POST /auth/confirm with the 6-digit email OTP is where the session and a PAT are issued. POST /auth/resend re-sends the code.
  • First workspace: POST /api/v1/workspaces calls bunkai_bootstrap_workspace (workspace + owner membership, one transaction). This is the one capability-free write a fresh token may do.
  • The active workspace for the browser is a cookie (POST /me/active-workspace, cookie-only); PAT callers pass the workspace explicitly.
  • Rules: the sign-in emails are sent by Supabase Auth, not by the app. Side effects: auth.users row, session cookies, PAT row when headless.

Flow: invite, join, remove and leave a workspace

  • Admin issues an invite (POST /workspaces/{id}/invites); RLS on workspace_invites is the permission check. The response carries the accept URL once. Admin may rotate or revoke.
  • Invitee signs in and posts the token to /api/v1/invites/accept. Order of checks: token exists, workspace live, then revoked / accepted / expired, then email match. Since 0118 the membership write happens in one transaction that re-validates the inviter under lock and fails closed.
  • Removing a teammate: DELETE /workspaces/{id}/members/{userId} (scope workspace:admin plus a live role read; works with a PAT). Ladder rule: an admin or owner may remove someone ranked below them; an admin cannot remove an owner (45221); nobody removes themselves through it (45220). One transaction unassigns the target's bugs (each audited as bug.unassigned), revokes their workspace-scoped tokens and the pending invites addressed to them, deletes the membership and audits member.removed.
  • Leaving (DELETE /workspaces/{id}/membership, cookie-only) runs bunkai_leave_workspace under the same member-row lock as removal: refused when it is the caller's only membership in a LIVE workspace or when the caller is the last active owner; on success deletes the membership and revokes the caller's tokens scoped to that workspace.
  • Business rules: owner is never an invite role; plan seat limits are shown on the billing page but not checked when inviting or accepting. Assigning a bug also locks the assignee's member row, so a bug cannot be assigned to someone being removed.

Flow: build the project structure

  • Create a project (POST /workspaces/{id}/projects): a plain RLS insert; the plan project-limit trigger (effective plan) can refuse it. A new project has no environments.
  • Create modules (POST /projects/{id}/modules), rename, re-describe or move them (PATCH /modules/{id}; events are written only for a real change), archive a subtree (DELETE /modules/{id}) and restore it (POST /modules/{id}/restore, see flow-archive-and-restore).
  • Add user stories to a module, edit or archive them (DELETE /user-stories/{id} also archives the story's criteria and ATCs), set status draft or ready_to_test.
  • Add, reorder, edit and archive criteria.
  • Rules: viewers cannot write; DELETE on modules, stories and criteria archives, never removes rows; structural module changes are audited.

Flow: import user stories from Jira

  • POST /api/v1/imports with a project and a JQL query (1 to 2,000 characters). Member or above; at most one queued or running import per project (409 import_in_progress). Returns 202 with the job id. The route now also checks that the workspace has a Jira connection.
  • A Vercel after() worker claims the job (queued to running), loads the WORKSPACE's own Jira credentials from the connection (no environment fallback; a missing connection fails the job as jira_not_connected), and pages Jira /rest/api/3/search/jql 100 issues at a time (at most 1,000 pages).
  • Per issue: description converted from Atlassian document format to Markdown (truncated above 50 KB with a marker), criteria extracted, module chosen by Jira component name or an auto-created "Inbox" module, then the story and its criteria are upserted keyed on the Jira key (external_id). Counts created / updated / skipped and per-issue errors are stored on the job.
  • Job ends completed, or failed on a Jira authentication error (including no connection) or any unexpected throw; it is never left running. Client polls GET /api/v1/imports/{id}.
  • One-way only: nothing is written back to Jira by the import.

Flow: author an ATC

  • POST /api/v1/atcs (scope atc:write) calls bunkai_create_atc: write gate on the project, project derived from the user story, every criterion must belong to that story (45020), the module must be in that story's module subtree (45021), at least one criterion, title and tag limits; slug minted; atc.created audited.
  • PATCH /api/v1/atcs/{id} calls bunkai_update_atc under a row lock with the expected version (45022 on conflict), replaces steps, assertions and bindings, bumps the version, audits atc.updated with the affected Tests. An archived ATC answers 45025.
  • POST /atcs/{id}/duplicate deep-copies into the same project with a fresh slug and version 1 (refused for an archived ATC).
  • DELETE /atcs/{id} archives and POST /atcs/{id}/restore restores (see flow-archive-and-restore).
  • POST /atcs/bulk-edit (scope atc:write): select ATCs, choose ONE field to change (tags add or remove, module, layer, priority), optionally dry-run to see refusals, then confirm. Up to 200 ATCs; the per-ATC outcome list says changed, unchanged or refused with a reason; one atc.updated event per changed ATC.
  • Reads: GET /atcs/{id}/usage, GET /atcs/search, GET /projects/{id}/atcs/export (CSV).
  • There is still no ATC hard delete; an ATC leaves the library through its own archive or a parent cascade.

Flow: compose Tests, plans and milestones

  • POST /api/v1/tests (Idempotency-Key header required: 400 idempotency_key_required without it) calls bunkai_create_test: write role, non-empty chain (45120), title rules (45121), every ATC in the caller's workspace (45122); test.created audited.
  • PATCH /tests/{id}/reorder and PUT /tests/{id}/tags, both version-guarded. Reads: expanded Test, run history, tag filter (keyset paged), search.
  • Test plans: POST /projects/{id}/test-plans creates an open plan (name 1 to 100 characters, unique per project ignoring case, goal up to 100, description up to 500). Edits only while open. POST /test-plans/{id}/tests adds Tests whose entire chain lies in the plan's project; DELETE …/tests/{testId} removes the membership only.
  • Plan progress is a read-only projection of run history: for each member Test the latest Run (greatest started_at then id, any executor, regardless of when the Test joined the plan) gives an outcome passed, failed, aborted, in_progress (a running Run) or not_run; the plan shows counts and passed percentage floor(passed / members x 100), null for an empty plan. Budget 200 members per plan.
  • Closing: POST /test-plans/{id}/close with a verdict passed or failed and an optional summary (plain text, up to 4,000 characters after trimming; whitespace only becomes none) freezes an open plan with the closer, time and the progress snapshot, audited test_plan.closed. Allowed for the plan's creator (if still able to write) or an admin or owner; a closed plan is not closable again (45603). POST /test-plans/{id}/reopen clears verdict, summary and snapshot and audits test_plan.reopened; history rows stay.
  • Milestones: POST /projects/{id}/milestones and PATCH /milestones/{id}; name unique per project ignoring case; target date from today up to 5 years ahead, re-checked only when the date changes. Plans are attached and detached through /projects/{id}/milestones/{milestoneId}/plans; readiness and archive rules are in entity-milestone.

Flow: execute a Test (Run)

  • Start. POST /api/v1/runs (scope run:execute) with Test, environment and a start_token. A browser caller is always recorded as human; a PAT caller may declare human, agent or ci, and the token id and name are snapshotted on the run. bunkai_create_run checks write role, executor mode (45200), environment in the Test's project (45201) and at least one executable step (45202). The same Test and start token within 24 hours returns the existing running Run. It then copies every chain position and ATC step as pending and audits run.started.
  • Mark steps. POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark with passed, failed or blocked, plus optional note and evidence URL. Only a running Run accepts marks (45212); pending is never accepted (45213). The run ATC verdict is recomputed on every mark. A bearer caller that repeats an identical result gets the stored result back and writes nothing (so a retry never extends the run's life); a different result for an already reported step is a 409 (45239). A person using the browser keeps last-write-wins correction. Each mark audits run_step.marked. Realtime pushes run_atcs and run_steps.
  • Evidence. Screenshots can be attached to a step while the Run is running (see flow-attach-evidence).
  • Finish. POST /runs/{id}/finish with verdict passed or failed (45207 otherwise): the verdict is the person's choice. Remaining pending steps and run ATCs become skipped, run.finished audited with via.
  • Abort. POST /runs/{id}/abort with a reason of 3 to 500 characters: status aborted, pending work skipped, run.aborted audited.
  • Finish and abort lock the Run row: the first terminal action wins, the loser gets 409 (45206 / 45204).
  • Silent runs. Human runs with no step activity for 4 hours are aborted by the 15-minute sweep; agent and ci runs with no step report for 60 minutes are aborted by a 5-minute sweep with reason "Inactivity timeout" (see state-run).
  • Automated submission, comparison and history flakiness: see flow-automated-run-submission, flow-compare-runs and flow-reports.
  • Business rules: every executor passes the same write gate; the Test template is never touched by a Run. Side effects: notification to the starter on finish or abort.

Flow: file and triage a bug

  • Optional evidence first: the filer uploads screenshots (POST /projects/{id}/bug-evidence to init, browser PUT, …/{attachmentId}/commit; DELETE discards an unclaimed upload). See entity-evidence-attachment.
  • POST /api/v1/bugs: with run_step_id the server derives project, module, run and ATC from that step; without it the caller supplies project and module. bunkai_create_bug validates module in project (45300), run in project (45305), step in run (45306), ATC in project (45307), title, severity and evidence (45303 to 45318 for uploads); the claimed uploads are attached in the requested order and frozen; status starts open; bug.filed audited.
  • PATCH /bugs/{id} corrects title, severity, description and steps to reproduce (bunkai_correct_bug): the caller sends the content_version it loaded and gets 45314 (409) if the defect changed since; audited bug.corrected. Status and assignee are independent of content.
  • POST /bugs/{id}/assign assigns, reassigns or unassigns: the assignee must be an active member (45312) and not a viewer (45313), and the assignee row is locked first. POST /bugs/{id}/status moves exactly one stage forward (45310 skipping, 45311 backward or unchanged).
  • Reads: project list (filters, keyset paging, severity-first sort), workspace-wide list GET /workspaces/{id}/bugs (all projects, most severe then most recent, with severity and status counts over the whole filtered set), single bug with origin and module archive tag, evidence content download, open-bug counts on Home. The Defect Heatmap refreshes through Realtime.
  • A non-member gets the same not-found as for a missing bug; a member without write role gets forbidden. Sending a bug to Jira is configured (entity-jira-connection) but not implemented.

Flow: notifications and daily digest

  • A lifecycle RPC writes its activity_log row. An AFTER INSERT trigger on that table (run events and bug events) computes recipients and inserts notifications rows in the same transaction. Chat mentions are written directly by bunkai_chat_sync_mentions (one mentions row per mentioned member).
  • Preferences are read at write time. The helper bunkai_notification_channel_enabled decides per recipient: in-app on stores a visible row; in-app off with email on stores a row flagged in_app_suppressed (no inbox, bell or realtime, still digested); both off stores nothing. Mentions ignore preferences (always in-app).
  • Recipients. Run finished or aborted: the run starter only, suppressed when the starter closed it from a browser session; a close through a PAT, the sweep or an unknown channel notifies even the starter. Bug assigned or reassigned: the new assignee only. Bug status changed: reporter and current assignee, never the person who made the change. Unassigned: nobody.
  • The inbox (GET /workspaces/{id}/notifications) shows the caller's visible rows of the last 90 days; new rows arrive by Supabase Realtime. Read one or all.
  • Digest: Vercel Cron calls GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 08:00 UTC with CRON_SECRET. bunkai_notification_digest_candidates returns unread notifications of the last 90 days for active members of live workspaces, excluding families whose email preference is off, and excluding email-only rows already emailed. Per user the route inserts a pending claim row for the UTC day, sends one email through Resend, marks the claim sent or failed, and after a successful send stamps emailed_at on that user's suppressed rows. A failed day is not retried.
  • Database counts of notifications by type were not re-measured on 2026-11-17.

Flow: quality reports

  • All reports are live, read-only RPCs over the tables above; any active member, viewers included, may read them; a project the caller cannot see answers not found.
  • Coverage (project and workspace). Per criterion: uncovered when no live ATC is bound; not_run when any bound ATC's most recent run result is anything other than passed or failed; otherwise executed. A failed ATC still counts as coverage. Per module: no_acs, uncovered, not_run or fully_covered. Changes: an ATC repeated in one Test chain now gets a deterministic state (a run stopped between positions no longer flips on a random tie); an ATC archived on its own stays evidence and a criterion bound only to archived ATCs is not "uncovered"; an archived ATC that never ran no longer holds a criterion at not_run; the workspace figure is ONE RPC (bunkai_report_workspace_coverage) instead of one call per project (the old fan-out failed with 500 above 60 projects).
  • Story traceability. One call returns a story's chain criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug.
  • Run report. A project's runs filtered by status, executor mode, module and date range with pass and fail totals, now also Manual and Automated totals (human = Manual; agent or ci = Automated) and context flags for the empty state. Workspace Runs index: GET /workspaces/{id}/runs, newest first, keyset paged, filters project, outcomes, environment name and execution mode, with passed, failed and blocked step counts per run.
  • Test run history with a flakiness signal: raw counts of sample, flips and aborted or skipped runs; the app applies a window of the last 10 runs, a minimum of 5, and bands at one third.
  • Plan progress and milestone readiness: see flow-compose-test-and-plan and entity-milestone.
  • Recovery cycles. Per user story, time from the first failing run to the first later all-passing run.
  • Defect heatmap. Bugs per active module for a 7, 30 or 90-day window with a week-over-week trend, refreshed by Realtime on new bugs. Workspace bug index: GET /workspaces/{id}/bugs.
  • Home widgets and search (six entity types) are unchanged.

Flow: manage environments

  1. List or add (/projects/{id}/environments): name 1 to 50 characters in the API (60 in the table), unique per project ignoring case.
  2. Rename or delete (/environments/{id}). Delete is a real row delete and is refused while any Run references the environment. An id from another workspace answers not found.

Projects that existed when runs shipped were seeded with Staging and Production; projects created later start with none, and a Run cannot start until one exists. Database: 1,736 of 1,866 projects have no environment.

Flow: upgrade to the Cloud plan

  • An admin or owner reads the plan overview (GET /workspaces/{id}/billing): plan, purchased seats, active seats, project count, oldest run age, and now whether a renewal is overdue; others get 404.
  • Owner only: POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout (idempotency key, PAT needs workspace:admin) inserts a billing_checkout_sessions row first, at most one open per workspace, then creates a Stripe Checkout Session with that row id as client_reference_id. A workspace with an unpaid renewal is refused (plan_not_upgradable, reason payment_overdue): it already has a subscription, so the way back is the payment method and the retry (see flow-billing-maintenance). …/checkout/cancel expires the Stripe session and marks the row canceled.
  • Stripe calls POST /api/v1/billing/webhook. Checkout events handled: checkout.session.completed, …async_payment_succeeded, …async_payment_failed, …expired; a Checkout Session in setup mode (payment-method replacement) is routed away from this path; invoice events are handled too (next flow). bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event finds the row, records the event id for dedupe, and only when Stripe reports paid sets the workspace plan to cloud and purchased_seats and records the customer and subscription mapping in workspace_billing_state. An unknown session answers 5xx so Stripe retries.
  • Database (2026-11-17): 1 workspace is on cloud, 8 enterprise, 3,096 community. There is still no downgrade or cancellation handling.

Flow: export workspace data

  1. Owner only, browser session only. POST /workspaces/{id}/data-export enqueues a job; one queued or running export per workspace. A trigger audits export.requested.
  2. A Vercel after() worker claims it, collects projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs with steps, assertions and bindings, Tests and chains, Runs with snapshots, bugs, activity and memberships, zips them and uploads to the private Storage bucket workspace-exports; the job becomes completed with size and an expiry 168 hours later, or failed with a message.
  3. GET …/data-export/download re-checks owner, completed and not expired on every request, streams the archive (never a signed URL) and audits export.downloaded.

Flow: delete and restore a workspace

  • Owner only, browser session only: DELETE /workspaces/{id} runs bunkai_request_workspace_deletion. Other members cannot veto. In one transaction: deleted_at set, all workspace-scoped PATs and pending invites revoked, a workspace_deletions tombstone written (name, slug, requester, purge deadline 30 days later, member count, row-count digest). A test-only failpoint (bunkai_test_failpoints, workspace_delete.before_return) lets an integration test force a failure after every write to prove the workspace stays intact.
  • After commit, a confirmation email with the restore link goes to the owner and every active member through Resend.
  • From that moment nobody, owner included, can read or write the workspace through any path; digests stop. Members' memberships stay active and do not count toward the "last membership" guard of Leave.
  • During the grace window the owner can POST /workspaces/{id}/restore: deleted_at cleared, no data moved. A restore after the 30-day deadline is refused with 45903 (restore_window_closed) even if the daily purge has not run yet: "purgeable" and "no longer restorable" are the same predicate. Revoked tokens and invites stay revoked.
  • The daily purge hard-deletes workspaces deleted 30 days ago or more; the cascade removes their data and the tombstone gets purged_at.
  • Database: 1,215 workspaces are currently soft-deleted (2026-11-17).

Flow: team chat

  • Read: GET /workspaces/{id}/chat/messages pages the general channel by seq; open browsers also receive Realtime inserts and updates; after a disconnect the client catches up by seq.
  • Send: POST …/chat/messages with body and optional mention ids runs bunkai_chat_send_message: caller must be an active member who can write (viewers cannot), the body is stored, mention ids are filtered to active members of the workspace, mention rows are written and one mentions notification per mentioned member is created.
  • Edit and delete: PATCH and DELETE …/chat/messages/{messageId}. Edit only by the author inside 15 minutes; the mention set is diffed (only added members are notified). Delete by the author or a moderator leaves an identical tombstone with an empty body; mention rows are removed.
  • Picker and links: GET …/chat/roster supplies member names (emails are not exposed to PostgREST); POST …/chat/entities/resolve and GET …/chat/entities/search build and find ATC, Test and Run cards (restricted or unavailable states never leak data).
  • Rules: no Bunkai chat feature crosses workspaces; the chat is membership-scoped, not capability-scoped, so a PAT scope does not gate it.

Flow: save and restore a filtered view

  • A person filters one of four surfaces (traceability, run history, bugs, workbench) of a project and saves the state under a name: POST /projects/{id}/saved-views.
  • The route validates the name (NFC-normalised, unique per person, project and surface) and the per-surface state shape; the database enforces uniqueness, the cap of 25 views per surface (45100), ownership and immutable columns regardless of the client.
  • List own views with GET, rename or replace state with PATCH /saved-views/{viewId}, remove with DELETE. Restore ignores unknown state keys, so a malformed own row only affects its owner.

Flow: manage billing details, invoices and a failed renewal

  • Details. Owner or admin read, the owner writes company name, billing email and address (/billing/details); each save is stored in workspace_billing_profiles and pushed to the Stripe Customer so invoices print it.
  • Invoices. GET /billing/invoices lists invoices and /billing/invoices/{invoiceId}/pdf downloads one; Stripe is the source of truth and nothing is mirrored in the database.
  • Payment method. POST /billing/payment-method (owner, Idempotency-Key required) returns a Stripe-hosted setup page; the card is typed there. The webhook records the new summary (brand, last four, expiry) and stamps payment_method_updated_at, which unlocks the retry.
  • Failed renewal. Stripe invoice.payment_failed for a renewal invoice (billing reason subscription cycle) sets payment_state payment_failed and opens a 14-day grace window from the FIRST failure; Stripe's own automatic retries never extend it. Paid limits hold strictly before the window ends; afterwards the effective plan is Community (limits such as the project cap apply) while the stored plan stays cloud and nothing is deleted.
  • Retry. POST /billing/retry (owner) pays the invoice that opened the grace window with the default method; three guards stop a duplicate charge (route idempotency key, atomic claim, Stripe idempotency key per attempt). The state becomes recovered only when Stripe answers paid (or invoice.paid arrives later); a decline or timeout releases the claim and leaves everything as it was.
  • Recovery is recorded only from the provider's confirmation. An invoice.paid older than the failure that opened the window never reopens or closes it (stale-event guard). Events for an unknown customer answer 5xx only while recent.

Flow: submit an automated run and stream its results

  • Two ways for CI or an agent to put results into Bunkai, both with a bearer token carrying run:execute.
  • One call: POST /api/v1/runs/submissions creates a Run that is already finished, with executor mode agent, the token as provenance (the token must be bound to a workspace, 45238; missing, revoked or foreign tokens 45237), per-step results, a verdict, an optional reported duration (the Run is backdated by it) and up to 20 evidence URLs. The submission must cover every chain position (45233), use known vocabulary (45232), valid positions (45234), a verdict consistent with the step results (45235) and bounded fields (45236). An optional idempotency key in the body (scoped per workspace, 24 hours counted from the key row's creation) returns the first Run for the same payload and 409 for a different one (45231). A rejected submission rolls back entirely and consumes no key.
  • Streaming: start the Run (POST /runs with the token), report each step with POST …/mark as it happens (identical retries are idempotent; a conflicting re-report is 409, 45239), then finish or abort. A Run with no step report for 60 minutes is closed by the agent sweep.
  • Both paths write run.started and run.finished audit rows and trigger the same notifications; every executor passes the same write gate (a viewer gets 403).
  • Database (2026-11-17): 81 agent and 27 ci runs among 4,684.

Flow: attach screenshot evidence to a step or a defect

  • Run step: POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/attachments (init: validates type, size and limits, creates a pending row, returns a signed upload URL); the browser PUTs the file to Storage; …/{attachmentId}/commit verifies the object (content sniffed as PNG, JPEG or WebP) and makes it visible; GET /runs/{id}/attachments lists the attachments of a Run; …/content streams the file; DELETE by the uploader while the Run runs.
  • Defect: the same three-step upload under /projects/{id}/bug-evidence, followed by filing the bug with the attachment ids (see flow-file-and-triage-bug); GET /bugs/{id}/evidence/{attachmentId}/content streams a claimed file to workspace members.
  • Failure: a Run that closes during the upload makes init, commit and remove fail with 45216; an upload not committed or not claimed in time expires and the daily cleanup removes the object (see state-evidence-attachment).

Flow: connect Jira and point a project at a Jira destination

  • An owner or admin connects the workspace: PUT /workspaces/{id}/jira-connection with site URL, email and token; any member can read the connection status (never the token); DELETE disconnects; …/check tests the credentials. Each change is audited.
  • An admin configures a project: PUT /projects/{id}/tracker-settings with destination key, issue type and on/off; …/check validates the destination against Jira using the workspace connection. If turning the sync on would queue existing bugs, the response asks for the exact count and the caller re-sends it to confirm; a different count means a bug was filed meanwhile and the save is rolled back (45413, 45414).
  • Today these two flows only configure: no worker reads bugs.sync_state to create Jira issues, so no bug leaves Bunkai. The import (flow-jira-import) uses the same connection.

Flow: archive and restore (Module, ATC, Milestone)

Archiving hides, never deletes, and every reader of reusable content filters on archived_at while relying on the rule "an archived parent means archived children".

EntityArchiveRestoreRule
Module subtreeDELETE /modules/{id}: module, descendants, stories, criteria and ATCs get one timestamp and one batch idPOST /modules/{id}/restore: exact inverse of that archive (batch id)Rows archived on their own or before 0117 are not brought back; module.archived / module.restored
User storyDELETE /user-stories/{id}: story, live criteria and ATCs, one timestamp (55000 if already archived)No story restoreComes back only through a Module restore of a batch that archived it
ATCDELETE /atcs/{id}: own archive, records archived_byPOST /atcs/{id}/restoreUnder an archived parent, restore hands the ATC to the parent's state; evidence reads still count it; edit or duplicate answers 45025
MilestonePOST /milestones/{id}/archivePOST /milestones/{id}/restoreArchived milestone is read-only; its name still blocks a new milestone (45508); no other table is touched

A change that alters nothing (archiving an already archived row) is a success without an event.

Flow: compare a Run with the previous one

  • GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/compare returns the viewed Run against the previous Run of the same Test and the same environment: the latest by (started_at, id) among passed, failed or aborted Runs that finished strictly before the viewed Run started.
  • A step is paired across Runs by the ATC occurrence key (run_atcs.source_atc_id plus the n-th copy of that ATC in the chain) and the exact step text; no step id is used because an ATC edit recreates its steps. One database function holds the status matrix, pairing, counts and order, so the page and the API read the same data.
  • Read-only and called with the caller's own session (an RLS function; the service role would bypass tenancy, so a caller without auth.uid() is refused). A missing Run, another workspace, a non-member or a deleted workspace is one 404.

State machine: Run

FromToEventEffects
(none)runningstart (bunkai_create_run)chain copied, all steps pending, run.started
(none)passed / failedautomated submission (bunkai_submit_automated_run)Run created already finished with per-step results, executor agent, backdated by the reported duration
runningpassedfinish with verdict passedfinished_at; pending steps and run ATCs to skipped; run.finished; starter notified unless self-closed in a browser
runningfailedfinish with verdict failedsame as passed
runningabortedabort with reason (person)abort_reason set; pending work skipped; run.aborted
runningabortedinactivity sweep for human runs (no step activity for 4 hours, job every 15 minutes)reason starts "Auto-closed by inactivity sweep"; via sweep; starter notified
runningabortedinactivity sweep for agent and ci runs (no step report for 60 minutes, job every 5 minutes)reason starts "Inactivity timeout"; via sweep; starter notified

Rules: only running accepts marks, finish, abort or attachments; terminal states are final (no reopen). A CHECK keeps abort_reason present exactly when status is aborted. The two sweeps never compete: an agent or ci run is closed by the 60-minute job long before 4 hours. Database (2026-11-17): 2,357 aborted, 1,282 passed, 1,045 failed, 0 running.

State machine: run step and run ATC verdict

Values for both: pending, passed, failed, blocked, skipped.

FromToEventEffects
pendingpassed / failed / blockedmark (person or agent)note, evidence, executed_at; verdict recomputed
passed / failed / blockedpassed / failed / blockedperson re-marks while the Run is runninglast write wins; verdict recomputed
passed / failed / blockedsame valuebearer caller repeats an identical resultno write; stored result returned; executed_at unchanged
passed / failed / blocked(unchanged)bearer caller reports a different resultrefused with 45239 (409)
pendingskippedRun finished, aborted or sweptno executed_at

Run ATC verdict: pending while any of its steps is pending; then failed if any step failed, else blocked if any is blocked, else passed; still-pending run ATCs become skipped when the Run closes.

State machine: Bug

FromToEventEffects
(none)openfilebug.filed
openin_progressstatus changebug.status_changed; reporter and assignee notified, never the actor
in_progressresolvedstatus changesame
resolvedclosedstatus changesame

Rules: one stage at a time, never backward, no reopen; enforced by bunkai_transition_bug_status and again by the consistency trigger. Assignment is orthogonal to status and allowed in any status. A content correction (title, severity, description, steps) is independent of the lifecycle: it works in any status and changes none. Home counts open and in_progress as "open bugs". Database (2026-11-17): 1,815 open, 758 in_progress, 203 resolved, 369 closed.

State machine: test plan

FromToEventEffects
(none)opencreatetest_plan.created

Rules: plans are editable only while open; closing a closed plan or reopening an open one is 45603; a missing verdict is 45604, an invalid one 45605; both functions lock the plan row, so the loser of a race gets 45603 and exactly one history entry exists. Database (2026-11-17): 25 open, 5 closed; the table still has no client write policy.

State machine: personal access token

Active until expires_at passes (expired, rejected with a uniform 401) or revoked_at is set (by the owner from a browser, by leaving the workspace, by being removed from it, or by workspace deletion). Both ends are final; rows are never deleted. Database counts were not re-measured on 2026-11-17.

Integration: Supabase

  • Postgres holds every business row; RLS plus SECURITY DEFINER RPCs carry the business rules. The QA inspection roles (qa_inspector_ro / _rw) bypass RLS and cannot read the secret tables (including workspace_jira_connections; a SELECT answers permission denied).
  • Auth owns users, sessions, magic links, email OTP and OAuth (GitHub, Google). Emails are looked up through two service-role-only functions because auth.users is not exposed.
  • Realtime publishes run_atcs, run_steps, notifications, chat_messages and bugs.
  • Storage: bucket workspace-exports (service role only) and the private bucket run-evidence for step and defect screenshots (10 MiB, PNG, JPEG, WebP, no client policy; signed upload URLs let the browser PUT directly).
  • Vault (supabase_vault) encrypts each workspace Jira API token; the table keeps only the secret id.
  • pg_cron runs four jobs: the run sweep, the agent-run sweep, the rate-limit sweep and the workspace purge. pg_net and http are not installed, so the database never calls out.
  • Failure behaviour: the whole product is down without Postgres or Auth; without Realtime, run pages, inbox, chat and the heatmap stop updating live but writes succeed; without Storage, exports and attachment uploads fail.

Integration: Stripe

  • Data out: a Checkout Session for the Cloud price with seat quantity and the session row id; a Stripe-hosted setup session for payment-method replacement; Customer updates from the billing details; a charge attempt on the failed renewal invoice; reads of invoices and invoice PDFs (nothing mirrored).
  • Data in: checkout events, invoice.payment_failed and invoice.paid, and setup-mode completion on the webhook, which change billing_checkout_sessions, workspace_billing_state, workspace_grace_periods, stripe_webhook_events and workspaces.plan / purchased_seats.
  • Dependent flows: flow-billing-upgrade, flow-billing-maintenance, state-billing-payment.
  • Failure: checkout start fails while Stripe is unreachable; a webhook for a session or customer not yet visible answers 5xx while the event is recent so Stripe redelivers; a delayed payment upgrades only when Stripe reports paid; a timed-out retry charge is reconciled by the later invoice.paid.

Integration: Resend

Outbound email only: the daily notification digest and the workspace deletion receipt with its restore link. Sign-in and confirmation emails come from Supabase Auth, and invites are not emailed. When Resend is not configured or fails, the sender returns a typed failure: the digest claim row is marked failed and the notifications stay unread; the deletion still happens without the email.

Integration: Jira Cloud

  • Data in: issues matched by the caller's JQL become user stories and acceptance criteria (flow-jira-import).
  • Credentials are per workspace (workspace_jira_connections, token in Vault); the platform-wide ATLASSIAN_* account is no longer used and there is no environment fallback. A missing connection fails an import as jira_not_connected; a Jira authentication failure fails the whole job; other per-issue failures are listed on the job.
  • Connection and destination checks call Jira from the app (flow-jira-connection-and-tracker).
  • Data out: none today. Bug sync state and destination settings exist, but nothing sends bugs to Jira. Stories keep external_id and external_url as the link back.

Integration: Vercel

  • Hosts the app; after() runs the import, export and deletion-email work after the response is sent; Vercel Cron triggers the daily digest (08:00 UTC) and the daily storage cleanup (03:00 UTC). Vercel registers crons from the production deployment only, so staging has no scheduled digest or cleanup (they are exercised with a manual call). If an after() task is lost, its job stays queued: nothing retries it.

Discovery gaps

  • Migration level: the ledger supabase_migrations.schema_migrations and cron.job are not readable by the QA role. The applied level was inferred from objects: 53 tables, 27 triggers and the newest functions and tables (chat, jira connections, evidence, billing state, bulk edit, workspace bug index) exist, so the database matches origin/staging through 0133. Numbers 0079, 0080 and 0102 do not exist in the snapshot; I could not verify whether the ledger has rows for them.
  • Environment: migration headers state that one Supabase project backs local, staging and production. I could not confirm from the database which environment label the dbhub connection represents.
  • Cron jobs: names and schedules (four pg_cron jobs) come from migration text only. Evidence the run sweep runs: thousands of aborted runs; I did not re-count the sweep reason on 2026-11-17.
  • Bug sync to Jira: bugs.sync_state, attempt counters and project_tracker_settings exist and a save can re-queue bugs as pending, but I found no worker or route that creates Jira issues; all 3,145 bugs are not_applicable and no project has tracker settings. Whether a later story ships the sender was not verified.
  • Workspace Jira connections: the table is unreadable by the QA role (permission denied), so the number of connected workspaces was not measured. Whether Vault holds the secrets was not verified (secret values are never read).
  • Earlier claim "PAT accepted only on a few routes" stays untrue; the route posture counts (107 handlers) were not re-measured after about 30 new routes (chat and settings are membership-scoped without a capability scope, member removal and connection writes need workspace:admin).
  • Earlier claim "no delete API": new routes archive or restore; removal of a member, a plan membership, an environment, an attachment and a Jira connection delete rows. ATCs, Tests, Runs, bugs, projects, milestones and test plans still have no hard delete.
  • 5 test plans are closed, but 0095 states that nothing before it could close a plan and every plan was open; how those 5 became closed is not verified. Closing now has a write path.
  • 13 Tests with an empty chain, and run ATCs stuck pending inside closed runs, were noted in the earlier snapshot; I did not re-check them.
  • 2 memberships with status suspended were noted earlier; no code writes suspended or invited; not re-checked.
  • Plan seat and retention limits are displayed as meters but I found no enforcement of seats (invites and acceptance do not check) or retention (nothing deletes old runs). The project limit is enforced.
  • Stripe: no subscription cancellation, downgrade or renewal-succeeded path beyond the failed-renewal grace; only one workspace is on cloud in this database.
  • Archived ATCs inside a Test chain: the Test read now marks them, but how run start treats an archived ATC in the chain was not verified.
  • Evidence limits per Run (250 MiB) and the expiry of pending run-step uploads were read from migration text, not exercised; Storage bucket policies were not inspected.
  • Chat: only the general channel exists (per-project channels were announced in a migration comment); message volume is 58 rows. Mention behaviour was read from SQL, not exercised.
  • Realtime: runs is still not in the publication, so a run closed elsewhere is not pushed; UI behaviour not verified.
  • Row counts of notification_digest_log, workspace_exports, feature_flags, workspace_billing_* and rate_limit_hits were not measured.
